step_3a_solver_parameters.verdict: ⚠️ QUALIFIED — two distinct solvers with different architectures serve different purposes

tag_positioning_solver.purpose: Per-frame tag trilateration against a FIXED anchor layout
tag_positioning_solver.algorithm: Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares (Gauss-Newton normal equations with Huber-weighted residuals, max 8 iterations, convergence at 0.02mm step, max step 500mm). NOT Levenberg-Marquardt — no lambda/damping parameter. The 3x3 Hessian is solved by direct Gaussian elimination (solve_3x3), not via scipy.

loss_function.note: huber_delta_mm is set from SolverConfig.solver_f_scale_mm (default 30.0mm). When huber_delta_mm > 0, the Huber weight is computed in ABSOLUTE residual space (mm), not normalized. Legacy path: when huber_delta_mm ≤ 0, falls back to huber_k (2.0) in normalized residual (residual/sigma) units.

delay_parameterization.anchor_delays: Per-anchor d_anchor_mm read from the Layout object (fixed, not optimized during tag positioning)
delay_parameterization.tag_delay: Per-tag or layout-wide tag_delay_mm (fixed, not optimized)
delay_parameterization.note: The tag solver does NOT estimate delays — it uses pre-calibrated delays from the AutoPos layout solve. The residual model is: pred = ||tag - anchor|| + d_anchor + d_tag

sigma_model.base_sigma: Per-anchor sigma_mm from layout (default 50mm, min clamped to min_sigma_mm=5mm)
sigma_model.quality_penalty: For T2+: inflates sigma by 1 + scale*(bad²), bad = (100-quality)/50, capped at 4.0×. Blends instantaneous and EMA quality 50/50.
sigma_model.residual_penalty: For T3+: inflates sigma further when residual_ema > 120mm (excess/80 * 0.5, capped at 2.5×).

temporal_prior.active_for: T3+ methods when x0 is available
temporal_prior.implementation: Isotropic Gaussian prior centered on last position, added as 3 rows to the normal equations (one per axis). For T4_V6_IMU_GATE, sigma is tightened by 1/sqrt(imu_prior_scale) when IMU indicates stationarity.

outlier_rejection.T4_method: solve_frame calls solve_once with exclude_index=-1 (use all). The C core does NOT do leave-one-out rejection in a loop — it solves once. The Python wrapper's T4 full-anchor path switches to T1 config (no memory) when n≥8.
outlier_rejection.reject_thresholds_unused: reject_abs_threshold_mm=120, reject_min_improvement_mm=20, reject_improvement_ratio=0.75 are CONFIGURED but the C solve_frame function only calls solve_once ONCE (with exclude_index=-1). These fields are vestigial or for a future rejection loop.

methods.T1_ROBUST_WLS: Base Huber-weighted LS. No quality/residual/temporal memory.
methods.T3_DYNAMIC_STABLE: T2 + residual EMA penalty + temporal prior.
methods.T4_NLOS_HEALTH: T3 + full-anchor frames use T1 (no memory). The production method.

autopos_layout_solver.purpose: Jointly estimate anchor 3D positions and per-anchor delays from inter-anchor range observations
autopos_layout_solver.algorithm: scipy.optimize.least_squares with loss='huber', f_scale=2.0, method='trf' (Trust Region Reflective), max_nfev=5000. The residual vector is hand-coded.

residual_function.range_residuals: (||x_i - x_j|| + d_i + d_j - measured_ij) / 15.0 for each pair

delay_parameterization.gauge: d_A = 0 (anchor A fixed as delay reference)
delay_parameterization.regularization: d_i / 20.0 added to residual vector (L2 penalty toward zero)

loss.note: f_scale is in NORMALIZED residual units (residual/15.0), so the effective Huber threshold on the raw range residual is 2.0 × 15.0 = 30mm

physical_priors.name: soft_two_layer_v1
constraints: D's z-offset from lower-ABC median: (z_D - z_lower_ref) / 180.0
E/F/G/H z-offsets from upper median: (z_EFGH - z_upper_ref) / 220.0 each

delay_parameterization.model: d_i = c + e_i (common mode c + per-anchor differential e_i)
delay_parameterization.gauge: NO d_A=0 gauge — all anchors float
delay_parameterization.default_behavior: When called with defaults, use_per_anchor_ei=False → pure common-mode (d_i = c for all, e_i=0)

loss.effective_f_scale: f_scale_mm / residual_sigma_mm = 2.0 (same effective threshold as v4-io)

step_3b_clean6_39mm.verdict: ⚠️ QUALIFIED — the 39mm is SELF-CONSISTENCY (internal pairwise range residual RMS), NOT rigid-alignment RMSE vs Vicon
step_3b_clean6_39mm.definition: RMS of (||X_i - X_j|| - M_ij) over all 15 clean-6 anchor pairs, where X_i are the MDS+Gauss-Newton solved positions and M_ij are the measured inter-anchor range medians

code_producing_39mm.fusion: undirected(med, a, b) at line 51-53: takes pre-computed per-direction medians, returns np.mean of up to 2 direction medians
code_producing_39mm.rms_computation: line 74-76: RMS of (||X_i - X_j|| - M_ij) over i<j pairs

code_producing_27mm.data_source: sweep_SW01_100_prewarm10_20260710_140144 (meta.datasets.field in diagnostic_summary.json — SAME physical sweep file)
code_producing_27mm.fusion: undirected_med(D, a, b) at line 70-72: pools ALL raw values from both directions into one list, returns statistics.median of the pooled list
code_producing_27mm.rms_computation: line 103-105: RMS of (||X_i - X_j|| - M_ij) over i<j pairs (identical formula)

significance.what_it_measures: How well a rigid geometry explains the pairwise range measurements. A 39mm self-consistency means the 15 inter-anchor ranges for ACDEFG are internally coherent to ~39mm RMS under best_effort_layout.py's range fusion.
significance.what_it_does_NOT_measure: Absolute positional accuracy. Two geometries with identical self-consistency can differ by a common-mode scale factor or coordinate-frame rotation. Self-consistency cannot detect common-mode delay bias.

best_effort_layout_py.method: np.mean of per-direction medians (med dict is pre-computed at line 46 as statistics.median per direction-key)

diagnostic_py_on_same_sweep.method: statistics.median of all raw values pooled from both directions (via undirected_vals at line 66-67)

fusion_method_discrepancy.additional_difference: GN iterations: best_effort uses 2000 (line 67), diagnostic uses 3000 (line 92)
fusion_method_discrepancy.explanation: The 12mm gap (39 vs 27.2) comes from different range-fusion methods applied to the same sweep file. np.mean-of-direction-medians preserves TX/RX asymmetry in each fused pair distance; statistics.median-of-pooled suppresses it. The GN iteration count difference (2000 vs 3000) may also contribute slightly.

values_across_sessions_diagnostic_pipeli.note: These are all from diagnostic.py's solve_mds using median-of-pooled fusion. The best_effort_layout.py pipeline would give different (higher) values on the same data due to its mean-of-direction-medians fusion.

docstring_assessment.classification: ⚠️ QUALIFIED — misleading cross-pipeline reference, not a stale value
docstring_assessment.explanation: The diagnostic.py docstring cites '39mm' from best_effort_layout.py, but the diagnostic pipeline itself computes 27.2mm (midday) / 57.7mm (evening) on the same/later data using a different fusion method. The docstring is not wrong about the number's existence, but it is misleading because a reader would expect it to match the diagnostic pipeline's own clean-6 RMS values, which it doesn't. This is a documentation hygiene issue, not a data bug.

step_3c_v4io_vs_commonmode.verdict: ❌ REFUTED — they differ in MORE than just delay parameterization

delay_parameterization.v4_io: d_A=0 gauge, 7 free delays bounded ±60mm, L2 regularization d_i/20
delay_parameterization.commonmode: d_i = c + e_i, no gauge, c bounded ±150mm, e_i bounded ±100mm (or pure c when use_per_anchor_ei=False)

residual_normalization.assessment: SAME in default, but commonmode has a configurable sigma

delay_regularization.assessment: DIFFERENT — v4-io pulls delays toward zero; pure commonmode has no per-anchor regularization at all

bounds.assessment: DIFFERENT — much wider bounds for common-mode

loss_and_f_scale.v4_io: huber, f_scale=2.0 (applied to normalized residuals → 30mm effective threshold)
loss_and_f_scale.commonmode: huber, f_scale = f_scale_mm / residual_sigma_mm = 30/15 = 2.0 (same effective threshold)

data_subsets.note: Both use the same fused pair distances (v3 fusion)

erlangen_official_results.note: The commonmode achieves lower pair RMSE (38.3 vs 48.2), likely because v4-io has C and D delays pinned at the +60mm bound, while commonmode absorbs the common bias into c=112mm and keeps differential e_i within ±15mm.

layout_displacement.note: The two layouts differ by ~110mm RMSE after Procrustes alignment. The delay difference (~75-100mm per anchor) compensates part of the position shift.

step_3d_layout_comparison.verdict: ⚠️ QUALIFIED — overnight layout is in a different solver framework (no-delay MDS), making direct mm comparison misleading

diagnostic_full8.note: Inflated by B and H; C, D, H delays pinned at +60mm bound

overnight_clean6.date: 2026-07-10 ~12:15 (overnight 1000 sets, rounds A-G only, no H)
overnight_clean6.solver: MDS + Gauss-Newton, NO delays, Procrustes-aligned to v4io_field_check
overnight_clean6.note: Different solver framework — no delay estimation. Delays in the file (d=0, 4.1, 28.9, ...) are COPIED from the v4io_field_check layout, not re-estimated.

overnight_besteffort.solver: Clean-6 MDS+GN + Huber multilateration for B,H against fixed clean-6

erlangen_v4io_vs_diagnostic_full8.interpretation: Large displacements (128-599mm) reflect BOTH genuine anchor movement/disturbance AND the solver being pulled by bad B/H data. F is most stable (129mm). H shows the largest shift (599mm), consistent with being bumped. C and D show +56/+31mm delay changes with C/D/H hitting the +60mm solver bound in the diagnostic solve — a sign the bad anchors are contaminating the delay estimates.
erlangen_v4io_vs_diagnostic_full8.caution: These are NOT physical anchor displacements — they conflate actual movement, solver-delay coupling, and the effect of degraded B/H data on the full-8 solve.

overnight_comparison_caveat.note: The overnight layout uses a fundamentally different solver (no-delay MDS+GN) and was built from different sweep data (1000-set overnight sweep with no H round). Direct mm comparison against the v4-io layout is MISLEADING because the delay-free solver absorbs range biases into position rather than delay. The overnight clean-6 self-consistency was 18.5mm (vs midday 27.2mm, evening 57.7mm), showing the rig was most stable in the early morning.

key_findings: ✅ VERIFIED: The tag positioning solver uses IRLS with Huber loss (delta=30mm), NOT Levenberg-Marquardt. The C core solves 3×3 normal equations by Gaussian elimination.
✅ VERIFIED: The autopos layout solver uses scipy least_squares with Huber loss (f_scale=2.0 on normalized residuals → 30mm effective), Trust Region Reflective method.
⚠️ QUALIFIED: Per-anchor delays bounded ±60mm in v4-io, with d_A=0 gauge and L2 regularization (d_i/20). Two anchors (C,D) hit the +60mm bound in the Erlangen official solve.
⚠️ QUALIFIED: The '39mm clean-6' metric is SELF-CONSISTENCY (internal range residual RMS), NOT a rigid-alignment RMSE vs Vicon ground truth. Self-consistency cannot detect common-mode bias.

⚠️ QUALIFIED: The '39mm' in diagnostic.py's docstring is from best_effort_layout.py (mean-of-direction-medians fusion), not the diagnostic pipeline which computes 27.2mm on the same midday sweep (median-of-pooled fusion). Misleading cross-pipeline reference.
❌ REFUTED: v4-io and v4-io-commonmode differ in delay parameterization, delay bounds, delay regularization, and number of gauge constraints — not ONLY in delay parameterization.

⚠️ QUALIFIED: Layout comparisons across sessions conflate physical anchor movement, solver-delay coupling, and data quality degradation. The 326mm RMSE between midday and evening 8-anchor solves is dominated by B/H contamination, not actual anchor movement.
